name: Bactrian
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Gholami, Saloumeh. 2010. Selected Features of Bactrian Grammar. PhD thesis, University of Goettingen (publ. Harrassowitz 2014) — the standard grammatical treatment; PDF not accessible.
earlier_scan.note: extinct epigraphic language; stress at best reconstructed (historical Iranian accent), likely not directly described

sources.citation: Sims-Williams, Nicholas. 1988. "Bactrian language". Encyclopaedia Iranica III/4, pp. 344-349 (online edition, last updated 2011-08-19).
sources.note: Historical-phonology paragraph: short *a, i, u 'generally well preserved in stressed syllables', 'in unstressed syllables they tend to be weakened or lost', and internal -o- replacing 'an earlier unstressed *a or *i' may be a reduced vowel [ə]; nothing on where the stress falls.

sources.citation: Gholami, Saloumeh. 2010 [online 2012]. Selected Features of Bactrian Grammar. Dissertation, Georg-August-Universität Göttingen (hdl 11858/00-1735-0000-000D-EF94-2; DOI 10.53846/goediss-1495).
sources.note: Ch. 2 'Historical phonology of Bactrian' (pp. 8-39) has sections on vowels, loss of vowels, final vowels, reduced vowel ǝ, but no stress/accent section; the only mention is fn. 108, p. 36 (p. 46): 'According to Sims-Williams, o in unstressed syllables, for example, in the preverbs φρο- and πορο, often represents the reduced vowel ǝ cf. Sims-Williams 1989a: 234.' No statement of stress position.

sources.citation: Sims-Williams, Nicholas. 2007. Bactrian Documents from Northern Afghanistan II: Letters and Buddhist Texts. London: Nour Foundation / Azimuth Editions (Corpus Inscriptionum Iranicarum II/III; Studies in the Khalili Collection III).
sources.note: Edition with glossary; 'stress'/'accent' occur only in glosses ('distress', 'mistress'); no phonological statement on word stress.

sources.citation: Sims-Williams, Nicholas. 2000. Bactrian Documents from Northern Afghanistan I: Legal and Economic Documents. Oxford: Nour Foundation / Oxford University Press (Studies in the Khalili Collection III).
sources.note: Edition with glossary; no phonological statement on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Henning, W. B. 1960. "The Bactrian inscription". Bulletin of the School of Oriental and African Studies 23(1): 47-55.
sources.note: Philological study of the Surkh Kotal inscription; only 'accented pronoun' (vs enclitic) and 'laid stress on' occur; nothing on word-stress placement.

sources.citation: Sims-Williams, Nicholas. 1989. "Bactrian". In Rüdiger Schmitt (ed.), Compendium Linguarum Iranicarum, 230-235. Wiesbaden: Reichert.

sources.note: The standard sketch; its phonology (p. 234) treats o in unstressed syllables as reduced ǝ per Gholami fn. 108, so it is the most likely place for an explicit remark on the position of the (reconstructed) Bactrian accent.
